title: Arsenic Dynamics in Physicochemically Heterogeneous Aerobic Aquifers Mediated by Redox Capacity
content:
Abstract

We provide an efficient reactive transport framework to assess arsenic (As) dynamics in physico-chemically heterogeneous aquifers upon representing the collective behavior of multiple redox-active sediment constituents through (measurable) electron accepting and electron donating capacities (EAC and EDC). This reduced-order representation is motivated by the difficulty of explicitly describing the various coupled redox reactions controlling the key transport processes in natural sediments. Laboratory-scale batch experiments show that the proposed framework can successfully characterize the observed evolution of arsenic speciation together with changes in sediment EAC and EDC. The ensuing (calibrated) kinetics are then employed to inform groundwater flow and transport simulations in a heterogeneous system containing low-permeability inclusions to investigate interplays between structural and chemical heterogeneity. Our results show that As breakthrough curves exhibit a non-monotonic response to heterogeneity characteristics. Global sensitivity analysis further reveals a stage-dependent transition in the main parameters controlling system behavior. Hydraulic heterogeneity is seen to govern the early transport-controlled behavior while sediment redox capacity dominates as reactions progressively become main controls on arsenic transformation. Our results suggest that the collective influence of multiple redox-active sediment constituents on arsenic transport can be effectively characterized through a representation grounded on electron accepting and electron donating capacities. As such, the proposed framework provides an efficient way of coupling sediment redox behavior with groundwater flow in heterogeneous aquifers while avoiding explicit representation of individual redox-active species.
